subject: Audit & Access Log Preservation — export formats, residency, and deletion proof request
messages:
From: Erin Walsh <erin.walsh@finacct.com>
To: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 3 Oct 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Audit / access log retention & export — legal Qs

Hi David (and Monica),

We're preparing a legal eDiscovery request and need to confirm Redwood's current capabilities and timelines around audit and access logs. Can you confirm the following for FinAcct's evaluation?

1) Retention windows by log type (management/audit logs vs access/authorization logs).
2) Whether we can get on-demand exports for a tenant (full historical slice) and the available file formats.
3) Residency constraints — if our tenant is in US region, can exports be pulled to an external party in EU/US and are there any approvals needed?
4) Deletion / erase proof — when a customer requests deletion of logs, what is the process, timeline, and do you provide a signed attestation that backups/snapshots containing the data are also purged?
5) Chain of custody / integrity — do exports include checksums or signing to support forensics?

If you have a short spec or sample export, that would be very helpful for our legal team. We may loop in our security/compliance lead (Raj Patel) depending on the answers.

Thanks,
Erin Walsh
Sr. Counsel, FinAcct Inc.
Attachments: none

From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
To: Erin Walsh <erin.walsh@finacct.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 3 Oct 2027 09:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Audit / access log retention & export — legal Qs

Hi Erin — thanks for the clear list. Answering each point at a high level; happy to jump on a call to walk through the details with your legal/security team. I've attached our short export spec (SOC2-audit-export-spec.pdf).

1) Retention windows
- Default hosted tenants: audit/event logs retained 90 days active; access/token events retained 30 days.
- Enterprise Dedicated / Reserved: configurable retention up to 7 years under an enterprise contract (we can set custom retention buckets per log category).
- Note: retention referred to above is for primary hot storage used by the platform for operational queries. Archived snapshots for long-term retention are kept per contract and can be delivered on request.

2) On-demand exports & formats
- Yes, we support on-demand full-slice exports for tenant IDs. Supported formats: NDJSON (newline-delimited JSON), gzipped JSON (.json.gz), and CSV for tabular fields.
- Delivery methods: presigned S3 PUT/GET links (for your storage), scp/sftp to a customer-designated host, or secure download link (short-lived) to a vetted recipient.
- Exports can be filtered by time range, log type, and resource id. Typical turnaround for a standard 90-day export is 24–48 hours; large historical slices (years) follow a scheduled extraction SLA we define per-job.

3) Residency & cross-border exports
- Exports originate from the region where the tenant resides (US in your case). We can transfer exports to recipients outside the region, but cross-border transfers require a documented data transfer justification and may trigger a review with our compliance team. For enterprise agreements we include a standard data export flow; for some regulated customers we keep exports within the same region unless explicitly authorized.

4) Deletion / erase proof
- Customer-initiated deletion flow: 1) immediate logical deletion in the tenant index (effective within 24 hours), 2) marked for purge from hot storage and placed into a 30-day quarantine (to allow for accidental restores), 3) physical purge processes run at the next maintenance window after quarantine.
- Backups & snapshots: backups are retained per backup retention policy (by default 90 days); permanent deletion from backups requires an enterprise change and specific schedule. We can provide a signed deletion attestation and a description of backup purge windows for contracted customers.

5) Chain of custody / integrity
- Exports include MD5 and SHA256 checksums for each file. For higher-assurance needs we can provide PGP-signed manifests or time-stamped audit receipts.

Next steps
- I've attached the SOC2 export spec. If you want a small sample export for format validation, we can generate a redacted sample (no PII) — let me know the time range.
- If FinAcct needs a deletion attestation template, we can draft one for legal review.

Best,
David Kim
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
Attachments: SOC2-audit-export-spec.pdf

From: Erin Walsh <erin.walsh@finacct.com>
To: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Raj Patel <raj.p@acmehealth.com>
Date: Mon, 4 Oct 2027 11:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Audit / access log retention & export — legal Qs

Thanks David — that helps a lot. A couple of follow-ups from legal/security:

• For the backup/snapshot purges, can you confirm whether backups are immutable (WORM) for a period and, if so, what change window is required to remove a file completely from all backups? Our regulator expects proof that when a deletion is requested for data subject rights, backups do not cause the data to persist beyond a certified removal date.

• For the cross-border transfer: what documentation do you require from our side to approve a transfer to our EU counsel? Standard DPAs? A signed export authorization?

• Please go ahead and produce a redacted sample export for tenant finacct-prod covering 2027-07-01 to 2027-09-30. We only need event-type, timestamp, user_id (pseudonymized) and outcome columns.

If you can provide those details by COB tomorrow, I can get them into our packet.

Erin

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Erin Walsh <erin.walsh@finacct.com>
Cc: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 5 Oct 2027 14:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Audit / access log retention & export — legal Qs

Erin — looping in Marissa from our compliance team to ensure we capture the formal attestation language FinAcct will need. Quick answers below, and we will follow up with formal documents.

• Backups / immutability: Our backups are immutable during their retention window; we operate incremental snapshots stored on immutable object storage with versioning. To fully purge a given data item from backups we run a targeted removal workflow which requires coordination with the SRE/backup owner; typical full removal (including removal from replication targets) completes within 30–90 days depending on the backup retention cycle agreed in the contract. We can provide a certificate of removal listing job IDs, timestamps, and checksums.

• Cross-border transfer approvals: For transfers to EU counsel we accept a signed export authorization form and a DPA in place that covers authorized recipients. If the export contains regulated data, we escalate to our privacy team and document the legal basis; we'll provide an approval record.

• Sample export: David — Marissa and I would coordinate generation of the redacted sample. Please include a manifest with SHA256 checksums. Expected delivery: we can produce the redacted sample and upload to a presigned S3 link by EOD Wednesday (2027-10-06) if FinAcct confirms the exact fields and pseudonymization approach.

We will prepare: (a) export sample (redacted), (b) deletion attestation template, and (c) a short data-transfer checklist for your legal team. Marissa will reach out to set a short technical handoff.

Regards,
Lauren Bishop
Head of Customer Compliance
Redwood Inference
